translation_en: Yahya narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. Sa‘id ibn Marwan narrated to me: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Rizmah narrated to us: Abu Salih, Salmawayh, informed us, saying: ‘Abd Allah narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Yazid, who said: Ibn Shihab informed me that ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told him that ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, began was true dreams during sleep. He never saw a dream except that it came true as clearly as the break of dawn. Then solitude was made beloved to him. He would go to the cave of Hira’ and devote himself to worship there—Ibn Shihab said: ‘Tahannuth’ means worship—for a number of nights before returning to his family. He would take provisions for this, then return to Khadijah and take provisions like them again. This continued until the Truth came to him suddenly while he was in the cave of Hira’. The angel came to him and said, ‘Read!’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘I cannot read.’ He said: ‘He seized me and pressed me until I was exhausted, then released me. He said, “Read!” I said, “I cannot read.” He seized me and pressed me a second time until I was exhausted, then released me. He said, “Read!” I said, “I cannot read.” He seized me and pressed me a third time until I was exhausted, then released me. Then he said, “Read in the name of your Lord who created; He created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen”’ (96:1–4), through His words, ‘He taught man what he did not know’ (96:5). The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, returned with these verses, his upper chest trembling, until he entered upon Khadijah and said, ‘Wrap me up, wrap me up!’ They wrapped him until his fear had passed. He said to Khadijah, ‘What is wrong with me? I feared for myself.’ He told her what had happened. Khadijah said, ‘Never! Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. By Allah, you maintain ties of kinship, speak truthfully, bear the burdens of the weak, provide for those who have nothing, honor guests, and help people through the hardships that befall them in the cause of truth.’ Khadijah then took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, her paternal cousin, the son of her father’s brother. During the pre-Islamic period, he had become a Christian. He used to write Arabic script and, as much as Allah willed, write from the Gospel in Arabic. He was an elderly man who had become blind. Khadijah said, ‘Cousin, listen to your nephew.’ Waraqah said, ‘Nephew, what have you seen?’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, told him what he had seen. Waraqah said, ‘This is the Namus—the one who brought revelation—whom Allah sent down to Musa. If only I were young during that time! If only I could be alive when your people drive you out!’ He mentioned something further. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Will they drive me out?’ Waraqah said, ‘Yes. No man has ever brought what you have brought without being treated with hostility. If I live to see your day, I will support you with strong support.’ Not long afterward, Waraqah died, and revelation paused for a time, until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, became sad.
